items.followUp: Explain why viruses are considered to lie at the boundary between living and non-living things.

rubric.why: Identifies their lack of cellular organization and their position in classification.
rubric.description: Viruses are acellular and are not placed in the five-kingdom classification.
rubric.how: Award for stating that viruses lack cellular organization and are excluded from the five-kingdom classification.

rubric.why: Identifies a non-living characteristic of viruses.
rubric.description: Outside a living host cell, viruses are inert and may be crystallized.
rubric.how: Award for describing their inert or crystallized state outside a host.

rubric.why: Identifies a living characteristic of viruses.
rubric.description: Inside a suitable host cell, viruses use the host's machinery to replicate.
rubric.how: Award for stating that viruses replicate or reproduce inside a host cell.

rubric.why: Identifies the basic components of a virus.
rubric.description: A virus consists of genetic material (DNA or RNA) enclosed in a protein coat.
rubric.how: Award for identifying genetic material and its protein coat.

modelAnswer: Viruses are acellular; they have no cytoplasm, nucleus or other cellular organization, so they are not placed in the five-kingdom classification.
Outside a living host cell, a virus is inert and may be crystallized, showing a non-living characteristic.
Inside a suitable host cell, it uses the host's machinery to replicate, showing a living characteristic.
A virus consists of genetic material (DNA or RNA) enclosed in a protein coat; therefore, viruses are regarded as being at the boundary between living and non-living things.

items.followUp: Compare simple diffusion and facilitated diffusion, giving one example of a substance transported by each.

rubric.why: States the shared direction and passive nature of both processes.
rubric.description: Both processes move substances down their concentration gradient without using ATP.
rubric.how: Award for stating that both move substances from higher to lower concentration without energy.

rubric.why: Distinguishes simple diffusion by its route across the membrane.
rubric.description: In simple diffusion, molecules pass directly through the lipid bilayer without a transport protein.
rubric.how: Award for describing direct passage through the lipid bilayer or stating that no transport protein is used.

rubric.why: Distinguishes facilitated diffusion by its use of membrane proteins.
rubric.description: Facilitated diffusion uses a specific channel or carrier protein.
rubric.how: Award for naming a channel, carrier or transport protein used in facilitated diffusion.

rubric.why: Summarizes the main difference between the two processes.
rubric.description: Facilitated diffusion requires a membrane protein, whereas simple diffusion does not.
rubric.how: Award for clearly contrasting the protein requirement in the two processes.

modelAnswer: Both diffusion and facilitated diffusion are passive processes: substances move from higher to lower concentration without using ATP.
In simple diffusion, small molecules pass directly through the cell membrane's lipid bilayer, without a transport protein.
In facilitated diffusion, a substance crosses the membrane down its concentration gradient through a specific channel or carrier protein.
Thus, the main difference is that facilitated diffusion requires a membrane protein, whereas simple diffusion does not.

items.followUp: Define biostatistics and state how it is used in biology.

rubric.why: Identifies the mathematical or statistical methods involved in biometry.
rubric.description: Biometry applies mathematical and statistical methods.
rubric.how: Award for mentioning the application of mathematical or statistical methods.

rubric.why: Specifies the biological subject matter to which the methods are applied.
rubric.description: These methods are applied to biological problems, data or phenomena.
rubric.how: Award for linking the methods to a biological subject.

modelAnswer: Biometry is the application of mathematical and statistical methods to biological problems.
It is used to measure and analyze biological data and phenomena.
